posts.title: Move-out cleaning in Gray Court before the holidays
posts.text:
Move out cleaning in Gray Court SC looks a little different in late November. Days are short, the ground is wet and a lot of families are trying to finish a move before the holidays, so the final walkthrough often happens in low light. That is exactly when streaks on glass and film on a stovetop show up.

If you are leaving a home near SC-101 or US-276, here is what to check once the boxes are out: inside the cabinets and closets, the fridge and freezer, the oven, the baseboards and the tracks of sliding doors. Most deposit disputes we hear about start with those spots, not with the big surfaces.

Our team cleans an empty home room by room so it is ready for the landlord, the buyer or the next family in Laurens County. The price depends on the size of the home and its condition, and we give it after a free in-home estimate.

posts.title: Why remodel dust lingers: Pelzer cleaning advice
posts.text:
Is the dust left after a remodel normal? In Pelzer SC, yes, and it is more stubborn than it looks. Drywall and sanding dust is fine enough to travel through the house, settle on shelves and slip into vents, and a quick vacuum mostly pushes it around.

Post construction cleaning in Pelzer SC works from the top down. We start with ceiling fans, light fixtures and window frames, then cabinets inside and out, then counters and bathrooms, and floors come last so dust does not fall back on a clean surface. Paint specks, adhesive and stickers come off the glass and fixtures by hand.

Whether you are finishing an older home near the Saluda River mill village or a new build along SC-20 or SC-8 in Anderson County, we walk the job with you before we price it. The cost depends on the square footage, how much dust and debris is left and how many trades are still on site, and you get the exact number after a free in-home estimate.
